name: Imnah
overview: Imnah was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified specifically as a son of Asher. He is noted in Scripture as one of the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt during the patriarchal migration. His descendants, known as the Imnites, are listed among the tribes of Israel in the wilderness period.
namesAndTitles: The name Imnah means "good fortune," reflecting a proper Hebrew name without indication of divine naming. This meaning provides a simple but positive connotation to his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Imnah as a son of Asher, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Imnah's significance lies primarily in his role as a progenitor within the tribe of Asher, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. His inclusion in the list of those who went to Egypt connects him to the larger narrative of Israel's sojourn there. The mention of the Imnites in the wilderness census further affirms his legacy within the nation of Israel.
